tone_patterns: Uses neutral, technical, audit-ready language with minimal adjectives.
Prioritizes definitional clarity (what is included/excluded, how calculated) over narrative commentary.
Employs directive, procedural phrasing for methodologies (stepwise instructions).
Separates descriptive statements from assurance statements to avoid conflating reported metrics with verified metrics.
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a dense quantitative table before introducing explanatory text.
Introduces a short bridging sentence that points the reader to a visual depiction of the metric breakdown.
Presents a compact reconciliation-style summary (starting population → exclusions → final reporting perimeter).
Includes a dedicated assurance paragraph that explains scope and standards, followed by clarifying limitations.
Ends with a methodology subsection using bullet steps and formula lines for each asset class/category.
heading_patterns: Uses a simple section header ('Metrics and targets') followed by subheads that label the purpose of each block (e.g., summary, approach).
Applies figure numbering and titles consistently (e.g., 'Figure X: [topic]').
Uses short, functional subhead titles (e.g., 'Calculation approach') rather than thematic headings.
table_patterns: Multi-column table with: category/sector label in first column and multiple metric columns to the right.
Column headers include units in parentheses and use consistent unit formatting across columns.
Includes a final 'TOTAL' row aggregating across categories.
Uses a dedicated column for a quality/coverage indicator (e.g., data quality score) alongside core metrics.
Aligns numeric values right; keeps category labels left-aligned.
Uses a symbol marker in or near the table to indicate items subject to assurance, with a legend elsewhere on the page.
figure_or_diagram_patterns: Uses at least two figures to complement tables: one for distribution by category and one for reconciliation/exclusion summary.
Figure titles are descriptive and mirror the terminology used in the table and narrative.
Reconciliation figure is structured as a step-down flow: starting balance → subtract exclusions → resulting reporting perimeter → breakdown by categories.
Figures are referenced implicitly by proximity and explicitly via numbered captions.
pdf_layout_patterns: Page begins with a full-width table occupying the upper portion, followed by narrative and figures below.
Footnotes are placed near the bottom of the page and keyed with bracketed indices.
Assurance marker symbol is explained in a short legend-style line near the relevant content block.
Figure captions appear directly beneath figures and use consistent numbering.
Uses clear visual separation between: (1) quantitative table, (2) reconciliation summary, (3) assurance note, (4) methodology formulas.
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses reconciliation language to define reporting boundaries (e.g., starting population, exclusions, final scope).
Explicitly states calculation conventions/adjustments via footnotes (e.g., treatment of negative values) without embedding them in the main narrative.
Assurance disclosure includes: type of assurance, standards followed, where the opinion can be accessed, and a limitation statement clarifying what is not assured.
Methodology disclosure uses consistent formula notation and defines denominators (e.g., enterprise value / equity+debt) by category.
Uses cross-references via footnote indices to clarify scope and definitions.
evidence_presentation_patterns: Pairs quantitative outputs with a data quality indicator to contextualize reliability.
Supports scope decisions with a structured exclusion list rather than prose justification.
Uses footnotes to document methodological assumptions and boundary conditions.
Separates calculation steps (bullets) from calculation expressions (standalone formula lines) for readability and audit traceability.
section_specific_observations: Combines three disclosure layers in one section: results (table), boundary/scoping (exclusion summary), and method (calculation approach).
Uses category-specific calculation approaches, each with a short step description followed by a formula tailored to that category.
Includes a coverage/portfolio-perimeter metric disclosed via footnote rather than in the main body.
things_to_avoid_copying: Any company name, auditor/assurance provider name, or website reference.
Any sector list, classification system name, or portfolio labels that could identify the reference entity.
Any numeric values, totals, percentages, currency units, or emissions quantities.
Any specific assurance standards cited verbatim; instead, describe standards generically unless required by the new report’s policy.
Any proprietary symbols or exact marker usage without adapting to the new report’s assurance legend conventions.
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Specific sector/category names and classification references.
All exposure, emissions, financed emissions, totals, and quality score values.
All currency and unit magnitudes and any portfolio coverage percentage.
Named assurance provider and the exact assurance standards referenced.
Figure numbers and titles as written, and any references to a specific report year or report title.
